tasks.short: Conduct practical classes and individual instruction

steps.what: Conduct classes, workshops, demonstrations and individual instruction in the subject

tasks.design: Keep practical demonstrations and individual coaching with the teacher. Existing instructions in the {DOCS} support the class without replacing supervision or teaching contact.
tasks.previous_blocker: Practical instruction depends on learners' actions and the equipment in front of them.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing digital materials can illustrate techniques but do not shorten this teaching boundary.
tasks.still_hard: Adapting a demonstration to different experience levels and maintaining safe practice.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher shows a technique, sees the attempt and adjusts the explanation.
tasks.altitude: The teacher retains subject expertise and the same instruction time.

reach.learn: Subject-specific setup and safe equipment handling

evidence.claim: Practical workshop instruction remains human work in this design; no measured or assumed contact-time saving is assigned.

assumptions: Boundary is practical class delivery. General instruction and equipment supervision may overlap other O*NET tasks; a roll-up must allocate the actual contact hours once, not add these descriptions.
Learners produce practice attempts directly. No structured readiness flag or automated action is assumed.
Existing native materials remain available. No new software, recording or upkeep is introduced, so incremental work is zero.
unknowns: Subjects taught, qualifications and practical risks
research_questions: Where do learners most need a repeated live demonstration?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and incremental=0. Group workshops and individual instruction both retain their teaching time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Teach and supervise safe equipment use

steps.what: Instruct and monitor students in equipment use and care to prevent injury

tasks.design: Retain direct equipment instruction and supervision. The teacher can consult approved instructions in the {DOCS}; no software clearance replaces an observed safe-use check.
tasks.previous_blocker: Unsafe handling needs immediate contextual intervention.
tasks.enabler_now: No technical change is required for the proposed boundary.
tasks.still_hard: Watching several learners while recognising an emerging equipment hazard.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher observes handling and stops unsafe practice promptly.
tasks.altitude: Safety responsibility and supervision time stay unchanged.

reach.task: Identify damaged practice equipment before use
reach.learn: Equipment-specific defect reporting and stop-use procedures

evidence.claim: Equipment instruction and live monitoring are retained rather than treated as automatable record work.

assumptions: Boundary is safe use during instruction, not a separate maintenance-record task. Overlapping workshop supervision must be owned once in the team roll-up.
Teacher observes equipment condition and student handling directly, using provider-approved instructions. There is no structured safe-use flag feeding a machine step.
Native document access is sufficient; no new capture, custom build or upkeep is introduced. Incremental work is zero.
unknowns: Equipment types and required supervision levels
research_questions: Which equipment situations require additional human supervision?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 and R=100; no incremental work. Routine demonstrations and unsafe-use interventions both retain all supervision time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Discuss children's progress with parents or guardians

steps.what: Meet with parents and guardians to discuss progress and determine their priorities

tasks.design: Keep the progress conversation with the teacher and authorised parent or guardian. Existing learning examples from the {DOCS} can inform it; recording, transcription and automatic progress claims are not introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Priorities emerge through discussion and may differ between child, teacher and guardian.
tasks.enabler_now: No technical change is needed within the conversation boundary.
tasks.still_hard: Explaining concerns respectfully and agreeing realistic priorities.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher listens, interprets examples and builds trust.
tasks.altitude: The relationship and decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Support a sensitive discussion about learning access

evidence.claim: Sensitive progress discussions retain teacher time; the digest's tutoring trials do not establish time savings for parent meetings.

assumptions: Boundary is focal teacher meeting time for courses involving children. Scheduling and any separately assigned reporting are excluded; adult-only courses may not perform this task.
Parent or guardian supplies priorities directly; teacher supplies existing observations and learner work. No structured progress score is required.
Other participants' time remains unchanged and is outside the focal denominator. Existing native notes are sufficient; no new capture or upkeep is added, so incremental work is zero.
research_questions: Do families leave with the same understanding of the agreed learning priorities?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 and R=100 for teacher meeting hours, with no incremental work. Routine updates and sensitive discussions both retain their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Gather class attendance patterns and practical scheduling constraints
Compare candidate class times against attendance and availability constraints
Choose and publish class times after checking attendance trade-offs

tasks.design: Start with native scheduling and attendance reports in the {OTHER} class-booking system. A deterministic comparison in the {SPREADSHEET} ranks feasible slots using explicit constraints; the teacher checks trade-offs and publishes the chosen schedule through the {OTHER}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Attendance and availability are compared manually across registers and calendars.
tasks.enabler_now: Class-booking systems already offer schedules and attendance reports; explicit slot comparisons can be added where needed.
tasks.still_hard: Past attendance does not establish future availability or justify excluding a small group.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher balances access, continuity and practical constraints rather than blindly taking the highest count.
tasks.altitude: Less repetitive slot comparison; the teacher retains scheduling decisions.

reach.task: Identify competing courses that share limited teaching space

evidence.claim: Momoyoga provides class schedules, online booking and attendance reports. The proposed constraint comparison and savings are separate E1 design assumptions.
Explicit feasible-slot comparisons can reduce repeated manual comparison without choosing the timetable autonomously.

assumptions: Boundary is focal teacher timetable work; no learner attendance gain is claimed as labour saving.

Teacher s1 checks and captures class ID, duration, capacity, room requirements, permitted dates, teacher availability, existing attendance counts by slot and any volunteered availability. Capture and correction retain all 35 hours.

Teacher or ordinary attendance registrar produces existing attendance marks as today, with no extra collection assumed. Room staff and colleagues maintain ordinary calendars as today. Missing or unreliable fields lead to manual comparison, not invented availability.
No new availability survey is required. If new collection is needed, its full time must be measured before applying this range.
Test native reports and scheduling first. Deterministic comparison reports counts and conflicts; teacher s2 interprets them. s3 retains decision, final schedule check and exceptions.
unknowns: Whether native reports cover feasible slots
research_questions: Does checked slot comparison save time after input capture and timetable exceptions are counted?

already_counted.description: Interpret candidate slots and investigate conflicts
Select, check and publish final timetable

incremental.description: Maintain slot constraints and comparison checks

approvals.approved_version: Exact class IDs, dates, times, durations, capacities and locations checked by the teacher before publication; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=35+17.5+24=76.5. Gross 23.5 less 1 upkeep gives net 22.5. Low assumes incomplete registers or native scheduling already removes comparison work; high needs this manual baseline and unchanged input capture within 35 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keep teaching, supervision and family discussions personal while reducing repeated timetable comparison.
reach: Discuss room conflicts and course access with an instructional coordinator
role.ambitious_version: Offer a carefully checked timetable that balances practical constraints and learner access without automating teaching decisions.
